name: Google Compute Engine G2 (NVIDIA L4)
price_basis: per L4 GPU-hour. g2-standard-8 = 1x L4 at $0.853624312/instance-hr. g2-standard-4 = 1x L4 at $0.706832276 (the cheapest L4 shape - 4 vCPU/16GiB per L4). g2-standard-96 = 8x L4 at $8.003330784 = $1.0004/L4. The 1yr/3yr CUD columns are consistent here: $0.5378/$0.3841 for g2-standard-8. Published 2026-10-03.
notes: THE CHEAPEST PUBLISHED L4 HOUR IN THE SLICE by a factor of ~2. $0.85/GPU-hr against $1.67 for the identical GPU on AWS g6 and $0.80 for Modal (which is serverless, a different unit). G2 is also the only accelerator-optimized family in this record set that shows a coherent CUD ladder across all its columns, so its discount depth is trustworthy: roughly 37% off at 1 year and 55% off at 3. The per-GPU rate rises slightly with node size ($0.71 at 4 vCPU up to $1.00 at 96 vCPU), the opposite of AWS g6 where the 8-GPU node is the cheap shape - so on GCP take the SMALL node. g2-standard-48 (4x L4) and -96 (8x L4) are the only shapes with a meaningful GPU count for multi-GPU work; the 1/2/4-GPU variants are really about CPU and RAM. Spot is N/A across the family. GPU-accelerated machines on GCP are billed for attached GPUs plus predefined vCPU, memory and bundled Local SSD - the G2 shapes have no bundled SSD, which is why they price so low.
